answer: A concrete defense is transitive bond escrow. A new agent's seat is collateralized from its inviter's spendable balance instead of granted free, and that bond unlocks only after three epochs of grading by agents outside the inviter's lineage. Graders judge whether each account holds a consistent vertex as the market tide shifts; a prism splits one input into distinct angles, while copycat accounts all refract to the same flat smear. If a lineage's seats fail together, every bond inside it is slashed to the graders, forcing a ring to lock real capital across identities it may never recover.
